Verified against frozen HEAD 3abee5a6add69443e49322e96f9130b834686235 and base 565def869ae50e47e6da7388ea333229050eaf8d. Structural counterexample: keep one Lazy invitation and one Live Watch run; start a passive append for context C0 and leave that promise unresolved, then successfully stream N distinct canonical contexts C1..CN. register.js:278-314 keys invitation duplicates by topic_revision/command_context_epoch and pushes a separate body for every changed context. onLine does not await pumpLazy; buildIo's stdout reader calls cb.line synchronously and continues reading (register.js:920-938). pumpLazy returns while appendInflight is true (:543-554), so the queue contains N+1 bodies for this single invitation. No timeout, coalescing, or pending-body count/byte limit occurs in the remainder of the module. If appends instead return deny, :568-572 retains current-run items and only delays retries. On recovery :546-554 frames all remaining passive revisions together. This yields history-dependent retained memory, linear duplicate searches per new revision, and a history-sized recovery allocation, even with a finite update sequence and no growth in canonical invitation count.
(a) Present elsewhere: canonical coalescing exists, but does not refute the downstream defect. invitation_content.rs:13-38 keeps a latest-context row; :1153-1175 resets the per-item counters on a changed context key, so the per-context offer limit is not a lifetime revision cap. Watch confirms the bounded canonical outbox after stdout write/flush (watch.rs:690-711), without awaiting mod append. It therefore permits each next context to reach this separate JS queue. invitationVersions' 1024-entry eviction (register.js:334-338) bounds successful-delivery bookkeeping only; dropQueued/discardStale (:144-161) act on lost runs, not obsolete contexts in a continuing run.
(b) Within contract: TRUST-POLICY.md:1554-1557 and :1658-1662 accept eventual latest context after quiescence, not preservation of every transient revision. A7's downstream silent-loss and the accepted render/deferral limits are separate boundaries; none specifies this same-invitation pending-body history as a tradeoff. Retaining an in-flight revision plus the latest pending context could preserve the stated delivery semantics. The finding does not demand progress while appends perpetually fail; it concerns unnecessary retained history accumulated before recovery.
(c) Scope: Q3 design:87-89 expressly excludes redesign of the existing daemon transport sink/queued notification frames and a new transport-memory cap. That exclusion does not cover the newly introduced invitation revision history in integrations/claude/mod/hooks/register.js. No finite session duration or practical revision/cardinality cap bounds this new history. Passive updates do not arm stall detection (mod_channels.rs:642-657); stalled_judgement also requires last_attention_push and an old pending ordinary receipt (:555-589), so a lone Lazy invitation supplies no forced channel-lifetime bound. The numerical epoch exhaustion limit is not a useful memory-cap mitigation. This is not a request for unlimited-scale delivery or a new transport API.
(d) Materiality: one pending invitation can consume memory and later model-visible context proportional to all streamed obsolete revisions, rather than the current decision context. Changed-context redisplay is part of this change's actual mod delivery path, and the same bug affects both a temporarily stalled append and repeated normal refusals. The risk is significant for a long-lived session; no external API failure behavior or undocumented engine size limit is needed for this conditional source-level proof. Severity Should-fix, not Blocking: it needs context changes during append trouble and does not establish an inevitable failure of healthy delivery.
(e) Pre-existing: base register.js:258 rejects invitation lines entirely; base :276-280 deduplicates supported queued items solely by ID, and base complete removes by ID. Although generic accumulation of different message IDs already exists, multiple pending bodies for one invitation across context changes are new/materially worsened here; preExisting does not apply. Current delivery.test.ts:1973-1997 and :2038-2058 explicitly establish retention of one newer whole/changed context during a manual unresolved append, but do not bound repeated newer changes.
(f) Linter territory: this is runtime retention/delivery behavior, not style or formatting. All six refutation attempts fail. No runtime commands or tests were run; the proof uses the actual module, canonical producer/Watch paths, named spec limits, and the base diff.
